decision_conditions: Wayfinding and signsPrior to occupation, details of the wayfinding and signage strategy, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Lee Valley Regional Park Authority. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To promote a sense of place and give mean while direction.

Cycle provisionPrior to occupation, the location and details of the minimum of secured and covered cycle parking spaces (for staff and costumers) and the indicative dockless bike location for the whole development outlined in red have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, meeting the requirements of the London Cycle Design Standards.Reason: to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes.

Delivery and Waste Management StrategyThe development shall not be occupied until a Delivery and Waste Management Strategy showing the full details of the waste and recycling facilities, including management of storage areas, internal collections and collection for the site for those accommodations, has been submitted and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The waste and recycling facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the relevant commercial element. They shall be retained throughout the lifetime of the development and shall be used for no other purposes.Reason: to encourage the sustainable management of waste, to ensure acceptable conditions for future occupiers in the interests of visual amenity.

Car parking management planPrior to occupation of the development, a Car Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will demonstrate how the Owner will allocate, provide and manage car parking provision, which will include:a.	A car park plan with clearly marked out spaces for loading, unloading, visitors, employees, accessible parking bays and parking bays for Car Clubs (as appropriate);b.	Details of measures ensuring parking is accessible to and available only for use by visitors and employees;c.	Contact details (telephone number, email, name) of a person/company responsible for managing of car parking;d.	Proposed parking controls to keep clear the turning areas for delivery/service vehicles;e.	Proposals for management of the risk of overspill parking; andf.	Details of parking allocation, enforcement, fees, maintenance and management.Reason: To ensure an appropriate level of car parking is provided for the development and to understand clearly the management strategy regards parking on site, to be convenient and accessible for future users.

Car parking provisionThe car parking spaces hereby approved shall be provided prior to the occupation of the development and retained in perpetuity.Reason: To ensure sufficient parking and accessible spaces.

Electrical vehicle charging pointsPrior to first occupation, details of siting, type and design of plugs, the energy sources and the strategy/management plan of supplying and maintaining the electric charging points to be provided in accordance with London Plan standards (passive and active), shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing.All electric charging points shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior tooccupation of the development and permanently maintained and retained.Reason: To comply with London Plan requirements.

Material palette and finishesPrior to the completion of surface lake of the above ground works of the relevant block, samples of all external finishing materials visible on the façade of the buildings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This shall include but not be limited to:i.	Facing and roof materials;ii.	Terrace treatment;iii.	Fenestration details including windows, doors iv.	Ground floor podium access, enclosures and gatesv.	All means of enclosure;vi.	External rainwater goods.vii.	Roof-mounted plant enclosuresviii.	Bin store and bike store doors/louvres, including level of visual permeabilityix.	Viewing platformx.	Campsite buildingsxi.	Ancillary buildingsSample PanelsSample panels of a typical structure bay shall be provided in proximity to the application site or at a location agreed and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Prior to commencement of above ground works, the sample panels must be approved in writing by the LPA and must show the brickwork, mortar mix, windows, reveals and window detailing, brickwork detailing, balcony detailing, balustrades, cills and copings. The sample panels shall be retained on site for the duration of the build.The sample board(s) required in (a) above shall be made available on site for consideration by the Local Planning Authority and approved sample board(s) shall be retained on site for the duration of the construction of the works to which they relate.The Development shall thereafter be carried out solely in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance in accordance with policy D4 and D9 of the London Plan, CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Policy (2014).

Operational and Events Management StrategyAn Operational and Events Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in full consultation with Strategic and Local Transport Authorities and the Lee Valley Regional Park Authority prior to occupation. This shall detail proposed arrangements for the use and coordination of the venue and the public areas of the site and, in particular, shall set out the measures for the safe management of visitor travel and car parking when multiple events are taking place within the application site and the wider Lee Valley Leisure Complex and shall provide detail of any noise mitigation.  This should also cover security related plans, procedures and measures in place, complying with the new Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025, emergency access and egress and ongoing training requirements of staff and contractors and ensure these plans fully integrate and comply with the wider LVLC processes, procedures and coordination, both during construction and all operational phases.An Event Management Coordination Manager shall be assigned 6 months prior to the opening of the Venue and shall attend all meetings arranged by the Lee Valley Regional Park Authority and manage, monitor, and pro-actively review the Plan and its operation in cooperation with the Local Planning Authority, the Lee Valley Regional Park Authority and other relevant stakeholders. This Manager should also be the point of contact linking into the wider coordination of the Lee Valley Leisure Complex.Reason: Traffic and transport implication and residential amenity.

Restriction UseNotwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) or any amending Order, the floor space provided to be provided as part of the approved development, including the Club house, the surface lake and camp site, shall only be used for these purposes and for no other purposes unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: Having regard to interests of amenity, design quality, impact on adjoining sites, traffic generation and the level of car parking available to support the development and the need to provide a mixed and balanced community.

Prior to first use of the site, details of the solar PV panels to be provided shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall deliver PVs as shown on plan ref 1197-0102-Site Plan - Roof Plan-PO2. Details shall include the specifications of the panels, the expected annual electricity generation and any constraints should clearly be outlined and marked up on a roof plan.Reason: To accord with London Plan Policy SI2 which seeks to maximise PV on all available roof space

Construction Logistics PlanPrior to the commencement of development, a detailed Construction and Logistics Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include:i.	A photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site;ii.	Works programme;iii.	Trip generation associated with the construction project, swept path analysis and identification of any works needed to the public highway;iv.	Routeing - primary and secondary designated routes to show how vehicles will keep to main routes and comply with the London Lorry Control Scheme;v.	Delivery scheduling;vi.	Use of holding areas and vehicle call up;vii.	Permit schemes and access;viii.	Parking, loading and unloading arrangements;ix.	Traffic management;x.	Details of contractor FORS membership.xi.	Measures to reduce Work Related Road Risk.xii.	Storage of construction materials, chemicals and equipmentxiii.	CLP management including contact details for the person responsible for ensuring compliance with the Plan during construction;xiv.	Provision of wheel cleaning facilities;xv.	Written confirmation that there will be no construction traffic access from Picketts Lock Lane.xvi.	Details of safe access for people walking or cycling across the site; access will be provided and maintained during all phases of construction; andVisual screeningxvii.	Details of how the existing W8 Bus Stop, the bus route and its users will not be impacted by the construction of the development.  The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan.Reason: In order to ensure that the impact of the development on the surrounding transport network is sufficiently assessed and where necessary appropriately mitigated in accordance with policy DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and Policy T7 of the London Plan (2021).

Night time ATZPrior to first occupation of the development, a Night-Time Active Travel Zone (ATZ) Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Strategy shall include details of:1.	Lighting: location, design, lux levels and operating hours of all pedestrian and cycle routes within the site to be included in the lighting plan.2.	Wayfinding and Accessibility: signage, surface treatments, and provision for inclusive access to ensure the routes are safe and legible after dark.3.	Security Measures: proposals for passive surveillance, CCTV (where appropriate), and landscaping designed to avoid creating hidden areas.4.	Maintenance: arrangements for the long-term upkeep of lighting, surfacing, signage and security features within the red line of the site.5.	The approved Strategy shall be implemented as agreed prior to first occupation.Reason: In the interest for pedestrian safety at night time.

Time LimitThe development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Canals and River Trust drainageNo contaminants including chemical and / or fuel run-off, shall enter the canal from surface water drainage during construction or operation. No surface water discharge to the waterway, including utilising any existing outfalls, is permitted without the written consent of the Canal & River Trust.Reason: To minimise risks of creating land instability from works to the cutting slope and the adjacent waterway during remediation of the site, construction and the lifetime of the proposed development in accordance with paragraphs 187, 196 and 197 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Secure By Design Metropolitan PoliceThe development hereby permitted shall not be operational until a Certificate of Compliance in accordance with SBD (Non Residential) Commercial Guide 2025 (or the relevant Secured by Design Guide(s) or an achieved Crime Prevention Standard) has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority, in consultation with the Metropolitan Police.The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained.Reason: In the interest of creating safer, secure, sustainable communities.

AMS and TPP (Trees)Notwithstanding any submitted plan or supporting documentation, no development, including demolition and preparatory work, shall commence until a scheme for the protection of the retained trees, in accordance with BS 5837:2012, including a tree protection plan (TPP) and an arboricultural method statement (AMS) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.The development shall thereafter be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: In the interests of protecting and enhancing tress visual amenity and the appearance and character of the site and locality.

Updated Energy StatementFollowing the practical completion of the development, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, reflecting the measures taken in practice in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of a development and its services, as committed to in the design stage, and the amended New Development Carbon Compensation to be paid for the remaining emissions.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets by renewable energy are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy SI 2 of the New London Plan 2021.

BREEAMThe development hereby approved shall achieve a BREEAM rating of 'Excellent' or higher or an equivalent independent measure of energy performance and sustainability. a)	A report from a licensed BREEAM assessor (or equivalent certification) confirming that the development has been completed in accordance with the required BREEAM rating and has maintained or exceeded the approved total credit scores for each of the Energy, Materials and Waste categories, shall be submitted and approved by the local planning authority within six months of first occupation of the development.b)	Following receipt of the post completion BREEAM certificate this will then be submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the development achieves the highest levels of sustainable design and construction in accordance with DMD51 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Whole life carbon cyclePrior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, the post-construction tab of the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment template should be completed in line with the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment Guidance. Together with any supporting information, it should be submitted to and approved by the LPA in writing.Reason: To ensure the development minimises carbon emissions throughout its whole life cycle in accordance with Policy SI2 in the London Plan 2021, Policy and the guidance set out in the Mayor of London's guidance 'Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessments' (March 2022).

Circular Economy StatementPrior to occupation, a report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority evidencing how the Circular Economy Goals and Commitments as set out in the approved Circular Economy Statement submitted with the planning application have been complied with.Reason: To ensure the development is resource efficient and maintains products and materials at their highest use for as long as possible in accordance with Policy SI7 in the London Plan 2021, and the guidance set out in the Mayor of London's guidance 'Circular Economy Statements' (March 2022).

Construction Environmental Management PlanPrior to the commencement of any development (excluding operations consisting of site clearance, archaeological investigations, investigations for assessing ground conditions, remedial work in respect of any contamination or other adverse ground conditions, diversion and laying of services, erection of any temporary means of enclosure, the temporary display of site notices or advertisements, a site-wide Framework Construction Environmental Management Plan and Code of Construction Practice shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The plan will include the following information:With respect to contaminated land and ground conditions:i.	relevant methods specified in CIRIA A Guide for Safe Working On Contaminated Sites when handling arisings, due to the potential for hydrocarbons, asbestos and other contaminants;ii.	procedures and protocols to prevent or manage the exposure of construction workers, visitors to the construction area, and users of neighbouring areas to contaminated materials;iii.	measures to limit dust generation during excavation, handling and storage of potentially contaminated materials;iv.	boundary monitoring of dust, volatile organic compounds and asbestos fibres during excavation and soil handling at points of greatest sensitivity;v.	appropriate procedures for handling and treatment of groundwater;vi.	measures to protect workers from vapours and dermal contact if hydrocarbonvii.	contamination is excavated, for instance during piling;viii.	measures required under the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 and associated code of practice;ix.	measures to control potential odours from the hydrocarbon and gasworks contaminated soils and prevent nuisance for workers and off site residents;x.	good practice operation and containment measures for storage of fuels or liquidxi.	chemicals to conform with government regulations and pollution prevention guidance (PPGs) issued by the EA; andxii.	measures required under EA Pollution Prevention Guidance on works in, near or over watercoursesxiii.	With respect to biodiversity:xiv.	risk assessment of potentially damaging construction activities, identification of biodiversity protection zones, practical measures (both physical measures and sensitive working practices) to avoid or reduce impacts during construction, the location and timing of sensitive works to avoid harm to biodiversity features, identify the times during construction when specialist ecologists need to be present on site to oversee works, responsible persons and lines of communication, use of protective fences, exclusion barriers and warning signs, details ofxv.	measures to control potential pollution events and sedimentation into the water course.xvi.	up to date ecological surveys of protected species and habitats, with a management plan for protection during and after constructionxvii.	measures required for the protection of the ecological corridor and other relevant environmental mitigation measuresxviii.	detail of the removal of the hard engineering elements of the water course and protection and safeguard measures to avoid excessive siltation of the water coursexix.	standard engineering safeguards, such as interceptor fencing will be installed where necessary to prevent laden silts and surface runoff entering neighbouring habitats, including the water course.xx.	neighbouring habitats will be safeguarded against accidental encroachment with appropriate fencing where appropriatexxi.	To prevent the spread of invasive non-native species, any other such species identified within or immediately adjacent to the Site during the construction works will be treated with caution and will be removed or avoided (with suitable barriers installed where necessary) as is deemed most appropriatexxii.	Lighting measures to ensure boundary habitats are not illuminatedxxiii.	Mammal ramps for open excavationsxxiv.	Timings to avoid nesting / breeding seasonsThe development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Construction Environmental Management Plan and Code of Construction Practice.Reason: To ensure the implementation of the development does not lead to damage to the existing highway, harm ecological features during the construction phase and to minimise disruption to neighbouring properties and the environment in accordance with policiesT7 of the London Plan, CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and policies DMD64, DMD65, DMD66, DMD68 and DMD70 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Hours of operationThe clubhouse shall only be open for business and working between the hours of 05:00 to 00:00 Monday to Sunday (including Bank Holidays).The surf lake and the activity park shall only be open for business and working between the hours of 06:00 to 23:00 Monday to Sunday (including Bank Holidays).Reason: To safeguard residential amenity.

LightingDetails of any external lighting to be provided including the design, height and siting shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority, prior to the commencement of works to any superstructure to include details of how bats will be safeguarded. The external lighting shall be provided prior to the occupation of the development and maintained at all times thereafter.Reason(s): To minimise light spill from the new development to existing residents and into the watercourse or adjacent river corridor habitat. Artificial lighting disrupts the natural diurnal rhythms of a range of wildlife using and inhabiting the river and its corridor habitat, and in particular is inhibitive to bats utilising the river corridor. This is in accordance with CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), DMD69 of the Development Management Document (2014) and EL27 of the Edmonton Leeside Area Action Plan.

Hours of operation for flood lightsThe surface lake and the activity park and their associated floodlighting shall only be used during the following hours:05:45 to 23:15 Monday to Sundays and Bank HolidaysThe flood lights shall be turned off when the surface lake and the activity park are not in use.Reason: To balance illuminating the sports facility for maximum use with the interest of neighbour amenity and ecology.

Community use agreementPrior to occupation, a Community Use Agreement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The agreement shall include details of pricing policy, hours of use, management responsibilities and a mechanism for review.  The development shall not be used otherwise than in strict compliance with the approved agreement.  The agreement shall apply to all the facilities on site and shall be available for community use in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To secure well managed safe, all-inclusive and accessible community access to the sports and leisure facility/facilities and to ensure sufficient benefit to the development of sport and to accord with Development Plan Policy.

Means of enclosureDetails of the proposed means of enclosure shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority Prior to commencement of above ground works. The proposed boundary treatments shall:A.	demonstrate how hedgehogs and other small mammals will be able to continue to travel across the site (such as 10cm2 gaps in appropriate places at the bottom of the fences); andB.	Any pedestrian or vehicular entrance gates erected shall be hung so as to not open outwards.The means of enclosure shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the development approved and permanently maintained and retained.Reason: To secure an acceptable design in the interest of visual amenity, to ensure that small mammals are able to move unhindered across the development site, and to avoid the unnecessary obstruction of the public highway in the interests of highway safety.

Artificial lighting to watercourseThere shall be no light spill from external artificial lighting into the watercourse or adjacent river corridor habitat. To achieve this the specification, location, and direction of external artificial lights should be such that the lighting levels within 8/5 metres of the top of bank of the watercourse are maintained at background levels. Background levels are taken to be a Lux level of 0-2.Reason(s): To minimise light spill from the new development into the watercourse or adjacent river corridor habitat. Artificial lighting disrupts the natural diurnal rhythms of a range of wildlife using and inhabiting the river and its corridor habitat, and in particular is inhibitive to bats utilising the river corridor. This is in accordance with CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD69 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Verification ReportPrior to any part of the permitted development being brought into use, a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation strategy and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met.Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete. This is in line with paragraph 187 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Dust ManagementPrior to the commencement of development, a Dust Management Plan (DMP), based on an Air Quality and Dust Risk Assessment (AQDRA), shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the local planning authority. The DMP shall be in accordance with The Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG 2014. The DMP will need to detail the measures to reduce the impacts during the construction phase. The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan.During each four construction sub-phases of the proposed development (demolition, earthworks, construction, and trackout), PM10 continuous monitoring shall be carried out on site.Parameters to be monitored, duration, locations and monitoring techniques must be approved in writing by the London Borough of Enfield prior to commencement of monitoring.Reason: To protect the local amenity from demolition/construction dust.

NRMM and plant powerPrior to the commencement of the development:a)	evidence of site registration at http://nrmm.london/ to allow continuing details of Non-Roadb)	Mobile Machinery (NRMM) and plant of net power between 37kW and 560 kW to be uploaded during the construction phase of the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.c)	Evidence that all plant and machinery to be used during the demolition and constructiond)	phases of the development shall meet Stage IV of EU Directive 97/68/ EC for both NOx ande)	PM emissions shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.f)	During the course of the demolitions, site preparation and construction phases, an inventory and emissions records for all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) shall be kept on site. The inventory shall demonstrate that all NRMM is regularly serviced and detail proof of emission limits for all equipment. All documentation shall be made available for inspection by Local Authority officers at all times until the completion of the development.Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and protecting public health.

Remediation StrategyNo development approved by this planning permission shall commence until a remediation strategy to deal with the risks associated with contamination of the site in respect of the development hereby permitted, has been submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. This strategy will include the following components:1.	The results of the site investigation and the detailed risk assessment referred to in the Phase I and Phase II (intrusive) Reports and, based on these, an options appraisal and remediation strategy giving full details of the remediation measures required and how they are to be undertaken.2.	A verification plan providing details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy in (1) are complete and identifying any requirements for longer-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action.Any changes to these components require the written consent of the local planning authority.The scheme shall be implemented as approved.Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, and is not put at, unacceptable risk from adversely affected unacceptable levels of harm to human health and water pollution in line with paragraphs 187, 196, and 197 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Unexpected/Unidentified Contamination Remediation StrategyIf, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site, then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to and is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site. This is in line with paragraphs 187, 196, and 197 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Acoustic ReportNo occupation of the development shall take place until an acoustic report, written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the operation of the site including combined mechanical plant and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the mechanical plant does not exceed the typical measured background noise level measured  or calculated as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest residential property.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance

Tree replacementIn total, no less than 796 trees shall be planted in accordance with arboricultural good practice in place of the tree to be removed/at a location to be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before planting, within one year of the removal of the trees hereby approved; such tree to be replaced with one of similar size and type should it die within five years of planting.Reason: To secure suitable replacement planting and to maintain the Borough's stock of amenity trees.

Gabion WallPrior to above ground works, details of the gabion wall shall be submitted to and agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Details shall include: 1. How the gabion wall would interface with the River Lee Navigation.2. Its exact location and relationship with the waterway.3. Its size.4. Its design.Reason: To limit any potential impacts on land stability and also minimise any existing landscaping and views from the waterway corridor / River Lee Navigation.

Landscape and ecological management planPrior to commencement of above ground works a landscape and ecological management plan, including long-term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for all landscaped areas, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority.The landscape and ecological management plan shall be carried out as approved and any subsequent variations shall be agreed in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall include the following elements:o	Details of any new habitat created on-site, complete with a full planting list composed of 100% native species across the site.o	Details of improvement works in the riparian zone of the Lee/Lea Navigation.o	Details of any maintenance regimes.o	Details of management responsibilities.o	Details of treatment of site boundaries and/or buffers around water bodieso	Details of retained or newly created habitats to include: o	Details of bat boxes.o	Details of nesting boxes.o	Details of bird boxes.o	Details of deadwood habitato	Details of otter hotls.o	Details of hedgehog boxes.o	Details of any other nesting boxesReason: The river basin management plan (RBMP) requires the restoration and enhancement of water bodies to prevent deterioration and promote their recovery. Without a landscape management plan, the proposal's ecological impact could lead to a further deterioration of the waterbody. This approach is supported by paragraphs 187 and 193 of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) which recognise that the planning system should conserve and enhance the environment by minimising impacts on and providing net gains for biodiversity.

New TreesPrior to occupation, a detailed tree planting strategy that includes, at minimum, the tree coverage shown in the approved plans shall be submitted with associated plans and standard planting details to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure all trees are planted with adequate conditions to meet maturity, support climate change adaptation and support biodiversity in the long term.Informative:The tree planting strategy shall detail:o	The key constraints and opportunities from the Soil Resource Plan and how tree plantingo	is adapted accordingly;o	The basis of tree planting proposals both aesthetically and how long-term growth ando	vitality will be supported;o	That species are selected that will reach maturity and be in proportion to buildings ando	open space at maturity;o	How trees will be incorporated into SUDS proposals and be complementary in designo	and function;o	Using recognised calculations, how soil volumes will be maximised and matched to theo	proposed species and site layout so that sufficient water and nutrients will be available to allo	trees at maturity;o	How subsurface engineering systems such as plastic crates or supports (e.g green blueo	urban, deep root) will be utilised, justified and minimised to ensure sustainable growth whileo	minimising underground complexity and reliance on plastics;o	How soil volumes in planting pits will be amalgamated appropriately to avoid undueo	competition between adjacent trees while enhancing shared soil space;o	How tree planting pit dimensions and positioning of trees will enable balanced rooto	growth into maturity;o	Each tree pit dimensions below ground, maximum possible soil volume, proposed soil volume, and required soil volume for the species.Advisory: Reference documents include TDAG - Trees in Hard Landscapes: A Guide for Delivery (2014), Tree Species Selection for Green Infrastructure: A Guide for Specifiers (2018), BS 8545:2014 Trees: from nursery to independence in the landscape: Recommendations. Trowbridge and Bassuk - Trees in the Urban Landscape: Site Assessment, Design and Installation. J. Urban - Up by Roots: Healthy Soils and Trees in the Built Environment

Canals and river trust Risk AssessmentNo development within 25 metres of the boundary of the land controlled by the Canal and River Trust shall take place unless and until a Risk Assessment and Method Statement has first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the proposed development can be safely carried out without adversely affecting the stability of the land (with particular regard to the cutting slope). This detail should include full details of any necessary mitigation measures, vibration monitoring etc.Thereafter the development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved details.Reason: This detail is required prior to commencement to minimise risks of creating land instability from works to the cutting slope and the adjacent waterway during remediation of the site, construction and the lifetime of the proposed development in accordance with paragraphs 187, 196 & 197 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

HMMPPrior to construction, a Habitat Maintenance and Management Plan shall be submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The HMMP shall include:1.	Details of existing habitats to be retained, protected, or enhanced, including plans and ecological baseline data.2.	Management objectives for each habitat type, including desired ecological outcomes and timeframes.3.	Prescriptions for habitat maintenance, including mowing regimes, invasive species control, planting schedules, and buffer zone protection.4.	Monitoring and review procedures, including frequency, methodology, and reporting requirements to the Local Planning Authority.5.	Roles and responsibilities for implementation and ongoing management, including contact details for the responsible party or land manager.6.	Contingency measures to address habitat degradation or failure to meet management objectives.The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat. Also, to secureopportunities for enhancing the site's nature conservation value in line with the NPPF, Policy CP36 of Enfield Core Strategy (2010), DMD76, 78, 79 and 81 of Development Management Document (2014) and Policy El12 of the Edmonton Leeside Area Action Plan (2020).

River RestorationThe development shall not commence until details of river improvements along the Enfield Ditch has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be in line with our DMD Policy 63 Requirements and best practice guidance (TRFCC River Restoration Manual) and shall include:a)	An options appraisal for river restoration activitiesb)	Robust explanation for proposed river improvementsc)	Specifications and information such as levels, planting, cross sections of proposed river improvementsd)	Management Plan for future maintenanceThe development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure the protection and improvement of watercourses in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 63, Enfield Blue-Green Strategy, Local Flood Risk Management Strategy, the Thames River Basin Management Plan and Policy SI5 of the London Plan.

Drain down strategyThe development shall not commence until details of the surface lake drain-down strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be in line with pollution prevention best practice and guidance and shall include:a)	Information on the pollution potential and filtration requirements of the  surf lake waterb)	The quantum of water draining down and subsequent storage requirements for thisc)	The frequency of drain-downd)	The discharge locationse)	Pollution prevention measures in placeReason: To ensure the protection and improvement of watercourses in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61 and 63, Enfield Blue-Green Strategy, Local Flood Risk Management Strategy, the Thames River Basin Management Plan and Policy SI5 of the London Plan.

SuDS strategyThe development shall not commence until a Sustainable Drainage Strategy for the whole development site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The details shall be based on the disposal of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system in accordance with the principles as set out in the Technical Guidance to the National Planning Policy Framework and should be in line with our DMD Policy SuDS Requirements:a)	Shall be designed to a 1 in 1 and 1 in 100 year storm event with the allowance for climate changeb)	Follow the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy and providing evidence of the potential for full infiltration SuDS and maximising above ground storagec)	Follow the SuDS management train by providing source control for the site, and a number of treatment phases corresponding to their pollution potentiald)	Maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation valuee)	The system must be designed to allow for flows that exceed the design capacity to be stored on site or conveyed off-site with minimum impactf)	Clear ownership, management and maintenance arrangements must be establishedg)	The details submitted shall include levels, sizing, cross sections and specifications for all drainage featuresReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

SuDs verificationPrior to occupation of the development, a Verification Report demonstrating that the approved SuDS and Flood Risk measures have been fully implemented shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This report must include:a)	As built drawings of the sustainable drainage systems including level information (if appropriate)b)	Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systemsc)	Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage featuresd)	A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similarReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF.

Ground water flood riskThe development shall not commence until a Groundwater Flood Risk Technical note is submitted to assess the impact of the proposed caisson building on groundwater should be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This shall include appropriate mitigation measures including avoidance, changes to floor levels, appropriate drainage measures, and appropriate basement construction.REASON: To minimise flood risk in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy and Policies SI12 of the London Plan, DMD Policy 59, 60 and 62, the SFRA and the NPPF.

Flood risk technical notePrior to the commencement of development, a Flood Risk Technical Note shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating:o	Finished floor levels are at least 300mm above the fluvial flood level, and 100mm above the surface water flood level for a 1 in 100 year plus climate change evento	The development does not increase flood risk elsewhere by ensuring no net loss of flood storage and that overland flow routes will not be obstructedREASON: To minimise flood risk in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy and Policies SI12 of the London Plan, DMD Policy 59, 60 and 62, the SFRA and the NPPF.

Water consumptionPrior to occupation, details of water efficiency, consumption and water harvesting using BREEAM WAT 01 credits shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To promote sustainable water consumption and efficiency practices.
description: Redevelopment of existing golf course and construction of a surfing complex comprising: (1) Outdoor surf lake (Use Class F2); (2) two-storey clubhouse including terraces, with cafe, surf shop, health and well-being facilities, changing facilities, offices (Use Class E), surfing operations and solar panels; (3) external plant, machine and store rooms structures for surf generation (Sui Generis); (4) renewal and alteration of existing campsite and the provision of additional accommodation and ancillary buildings (Sui Generis) with communal space;  (5) use of land for pop up temporary outdoor events, with associated temporary structures; (6) free standing shelter with viewing deck; (7) engineering works including mounding and bunds; (8) public park, view point structure, pavilion and external play areas; (9) Pop up seasonal structures; (10) leisure facilities involving a pump track, skate bowl, sports courts, skate routes and external play areas; and (11) associated soft and hard landscaping, boundaries, lighting, flood lighting, parking and access routes.
